intentions.title: Let operators support outside users through a low-trust, named ticket-key credential that rides the existing api_tokens infrastructure but is kind-fenced inert everywhere else
intentions.evidence: keys.ex: kind=="ticket" tokens reuse ApiToken hashing/revocation/expiry but Auth.verify_token/1 filters kind=="api" so RequireToken/RequireAdmin/session auth reject them; permissions=["ticket"] satisfies no global tier; bptk_ prefix, raw shown once at mint.

intentions.title: Give the operator a triage-first Studio inbox (needs answer / waiting on them / recently closed) so the oldest-waiting submitter always surfaces first
intentions.evidence: triage.ex sort_key buckets open(0)/answered(1)/closed(2), open sorted oldest-waiting-first, answered/closed newest-first; inbox_live.ex renders the three partitions via InboxPresenter; plugin-owned LiveView at /tickets with :admin live_session.

intentions.title: Guarantee one lifecycle orchestration for ticket answer/close shared by both the HTTP operator surface and the Studio inbox, so a Studio action always emits the same semantic mutation event a webhook consumer sees
intentions.evidence: thread.ex operator_answer/operator_close called identically from TicketsController and InboxLive; emit_event/2 is the single public emitter (referenced against MEMORY error-emitters-duplicated); status is derived via transition/2, never client-set.

intentions.title: Make a leaked or hostile ticket key harmless: bounded thread growth, bounded message/attachment size, fail-closed ownership scoping that never leaks existence via 403 vs 404
intentions.evidence: thread.ex caps @max_messages 200, @max_body_bytes 65536, @max_attachments_per_message 10; owned_by_key?/2 + get_for_key/2 return {:error,:not_found} for foreign or missing ids (never 403, no probing); keys.ex verify/1 folds revoked/expired/wrong-kind into one :unauthorized while paused is distinguishable (403).

intentions.title: Get a new ticket key from mint to a working first ticket in about two minutes with zero custom tooling, via a golden-tested, pure handoff card of copy-pasteable curl commands
intentions.evidence: handoff.ex card/2 is a pure string builder (no DB/config/clock) golden-tested in handoff_test.exs; three curl commands (file, list, read) plus etiquette note; inbox_live.ex key-management view shows the one-time secret + handoff card on mint.

intentions.title: Keep the ticket/ticket-key CLI manifest honest: only verbs a real bp credential can execute are advertised, and the operator's 'answer & close' UX is a first-class flag
intentions.evidence: cli.ex: submitter verbs (ls/file/reply) are deliberately NOT advertised because bptk_ bearers project tier none and operator bearers 401 on :ticket_key routes; ticket.answer command exposes a --close flag; mint/rotate default_output "table" so the one-time secret is visible.

intentions.title: Treat ticket attachments as the hostile-upload surface: verify file type by magic bytes only, never client-declared MIME or extension, independent of the global media allowlist
intentions.evidence: attachments.ex sniff/1 derives MIME from magic bytes; allow?/1 checks a charter allowlist (png/jpeg/gif/webp/pdf/txt/log/zip); validate/2 returns typed :too_large/:mime_spoofed/:mime_not_allowed; linked_asset/4 scopes retrieval to the presented ticket only.
